title: Tier-aware regional routing with quota-prioritized admission
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Users across free/paid/enterprise plans sometimes experience surprising latency and errors when regional capacity is constrained. Current router sends requests by simple plan-priority then region affinity; when a region is saturated we do blunt failover to other regions or lower-quality model variants which causes cost spikes or degraded quality for high-value customers. This ticket proposes a quota-aware admission layer that: (1) enforces per-plan soft reserves and graceful demotion windows, (2) prioritizes within-region routing based on remaining quota velocity, and (3) selects fallback model variants with a quality/cost ladder instead of binary switches. Goal is to keep enterprise SLAs intact, reduce noisy spillover that affects paid customers, and limit cross-region egress/latency surprises for free-tier traffic.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Tier Admission Controller (TAC) between the request broker and region selector. TAC maintains a rolling consumption window per tenant-plan and a smoothed remaining budget metric. Admission scoring = weighted sum( plan_priority_score, region_affinity_boost, smoothed_quota_fraction, recent_latency_penalty ). Use soft-reserve buckets: reserve X% capacity per enterprise, Y% for paid, remaining for free with preemption rules that only fire when enterprise demand exceeds reserve for > T seconds. When capacity insufficient, the TAC will attempt the following ordered actions: 1) route to nearest healthy region with available soft reserve, 2) route to a compatible lower-cost model variant (quantized or smaller architecture) if quality loss within threshold, 3) add to a short-lived delayed queue with SLA-aware max wait, 4) finally reject with a structured error including suggested retry-after and recommended plan upgrade. Implement quota smoothing by exponentially-weighted moving average over 5 minute and 1-hour windows to avoid immediate hard demotion on short bursts. Provide config knobs per customer-class in Console (reserve fractions, preemption window, fallback ladder).
design_discussion: Trade-offs considered: 1) Hard per-tenant caps are simple but cause sudden rejects — we chose soft reserves for graceful behavior. 2) Cross-region routing reduces tail latency but increases egress cost; the TAC exposes cost budget thresholds so commercial teams can opt-in enterprises for cross-region failovers. 3) Model variant ladder makes observable quality regressions — we will couple this with Canary rollout and per-prompt eval hooks in Optimize. Implementation constraints: keep the admission decision path sub-millisecond in hot path; precompute smoothed_quota_fraction in a streaming aggregator (Kafka + RocksDB local store) to avoid RPCs. Security: no new data plane exposures, but telemetry includes tenant IDs and plan class in logs — must ensure PII redaction and audit controls. Monitoring: add SLOs for admission latency, demotion rate by plan, and fallback-quality delta on sampled requests.
acceptance_criteria: Admission path adds < 0.8ms median overhead in production microbenchmarks
Enterprise demotion rate < 0.05% under normal load and < 1% during outages
Paid plan latency tail (p99) does not regress > 10% after rollout
Fallback ladder selection annotated in logs and visible in Console with counts by model variant
Automated tests for preemption window and quota smoothing edge cases
Runbook updated with steps to override soft-reserve and emergency throttle
